extraction.quantity: Hall thruster type and magnetic circuit
extraction.value: annular-cavity HET; cylindrical SmCo permanent magnet at the radial centre and annular SmCo magnet at the periphery, iron (labelled SC45C) behind the magnets forming the circuit; no electromagnet coil
extraction.note: Permanent-magnet circuit: no coil-current B(z) control (contrast owner answer row 78, H-1 EM only).

extraction.value: stainless-steel cavity, inner wall coated with an insulator (silicone resin) against short circuit; stainless-steel anode located behind the peak-field region; Al2O3 parts at the exit face (Fig. 2)
extraction.locator: p. 4 text (stainless steel, silicone resin, anode position); Fig. 2 labels (Al2O3); Fig. 5 caption p. 8 (grade SUS304)
extraction.note: The grade SUS304 is named only in the Fig. 5 caption (p. 8) for 'the sputtered stainless steel'; applying it to the HET anode/cavity is this lane's inference (verify).

extraction.quantity: peak radial magnetic field in the cavity (calculated)
extraction.note: Authors' magnetostatic calculation, not a measured map.

extraction.value: four holes on an anode electrode

extraction.note: No thrust, mass, power class or name of the HET is given.

extraction.value: pyrex tube, 6.5 cm inner diameter (65 mm, p. 6)
double-turn loop antenna wound on the tube; antenna covered by insulator and grounded metallic structures to minimize parasitic discharge outside the source (ref. [21])
extraction.note: Antenna axial position along the tube is shown only schematically (Fig. 1a/1b).

extraction.quantity: position relative to the thruster exit
extraction.value: the upstream side of the source tube is terminated by the HET structure; z = 0 is the HET exit and the tube / ion collector extends to z = 10 cm (Fig. 1a annotations)
extraction.locator: p. 2 text; p. 3 text (z = 0 definition); Fig. 1a
extraction.note: Coaxial downstream topology: the Hall exhaust passes through the ICP tube.

extraction.value: C-type stainless-steel electrode, 10 cm axial length, on the inner wall of the source tube, with an axial slit so that the RF fields can penetrate; collects ions to keep charge neutrality while electrons are extracted
extraction.note: The discharge voltage V_D is applied between the HET anode and this electrode.

extraction.quantity: applied magnetic field of the ICP source
extraction.note: No ICP magnet is described (unmagnetized ICP); the HET permanent-magnet fringe field in the tube is shown only up to z ~ +10 mm in Fig. 2.

extraction.quantity: RF generator rating and forward power used
extraction.note: Forward power 200 W; 'no power reflection is detected; the input power P_rf to the load is equal to the forward power of 200 W' (p. 3).
Reported as 'not detected' by the generator power meters (resolution not stated).

extraction.value: two variable capacitors tuned to minimize reflection; forward/reflected power from the generator's power meters; vacuum feedthrough to the antenna

extraction.note: From the RF antenna current measured with a high-frequency current sensor (p. 3).

extraction.quantity: total resistance during discharge R_total at P_rf = 200 W
RF power transfer efficiency eta_p = R_p / (R_p + R_ant)
extraction.note: Authors' evaluation of Eq. (1) with R_p = R_total - R_ant.

extraction.quantity: RF power absorbed by the plasma
extraction.note: = eta_p x 200 W; 'most of the rf power is considered to be consumed for heating the electrode' (eddy currents in the ion-collecting electrode; heating visible even without plasma).

extraction.quantity: authors' projection: RF power needed at eta_p = 80 %
extraction.note: A projection, not a measurement; not usable as a Vyovrinda power value.

extraction.value: argon only (proof of principle)
extraction.note: Single gas feed through the HET anode; the ICP re-uses the gas ejected from the HET (no separate ICP feed).

extraction.value: 70 sccm (2.1 mg/s)
extraction.note: Shared by HET and ICP; the ICP share is not separable.

extraction.value: 1 m diameter x 2 m long, three turbomolecular pumping systems

extraction.note: Gauge type / location not stated.

extraction.quantity: neutral density estimate in the 65 mm tube
extraction.note: From mdot = M n v S with an assumed v_n ~ 400 m/s.

extraction.quantity: CEX mean free path estimate in the tube
extraction.note: Assumed CEX cross-section 1e-18 m^2; shorter than the 10 cm source length.

extraction.value: DC supply V_D between HET anode and the ICP ion-collecting electrode; isolation transformer isolates the supply from the grounded chamber ('ensuring the zero net current to the chamber'); 50 ohm series resistor (arc limiting) and a 13.56 MHz L-C resonance circuit (RF interference) in series
extraction.note: There is no separate collector-bias supply: the collector sits at the negative end of V_D and floats relative to ground (V_K in Fig. 4a).

extraction.quantity: effective anode-cathode voltage reduced by the 50 ohm resistor drop
extraction.value: qualitative: 'the effectively applied voltage between the cathode and anode is reduced by the voltage drop at the 50 ohm resistor'
extraction.note: Stated qualitatively; see derived ID-R drop in the digitized table.

extraction.value: not induced for any V_D
extraction.note: Authors: implies the electrons extracted from the ICP sustain the HET discharge.

extraction.value: about 1
extraction.note: Digitized series: see digitized_fig4.

extraction.value: both increase with V_D and are fairly constant for V_D > ~200 V; the current limit 'seems to be decided by the rf power of the ICP neutralizer'
extraction.note: The RF-power attribution is the authors' interpretation (no RF-power scan shown).

extraction.value: V_max saturates at about 120-130 V and agrees with V_A
extraction.note: V_A squares are largely hidden behind the V_max circles in Fig. 4a and are not digitized here.

extraction.value: decreases to about -100 V with increasing V_D
extraction.note: Digitized series: see digitized_fig4.

extraction.value: qualitative: RFEA IEDF at z = 25 cm shows ions with maximum energy close to the anode potential with the supply isolated from ground (zero net current to the chamber); no electron-current or beam-current balance is reported
extraction.note: No separate measurement of the electron current emitted into the beam versus drawn to the anode.

extraction.value: four grids + collector at z = 25 cm on axis; 10 mm entrance orifice in a grounded cover (G1); G2 and G4 at -80 V; G3 swept 0 to ~400 V; collector to ground through a resistor, isolation amplifier gain 100, 1 kHz low-pass; 14-bit DAQ
V_D = 0: peaks at V_G3 ~ 20 V (local plasma potential) and ~ 40 V (ions from the source, plasma potential inside the tube ~40 V); V_D on: broadened component ~50-120 V
RFEA collector current at V_G3 = 60 V (zero at V_D = 0), a qualitative local flux of ions accelerated from the HET

extraction.note: No thrust stand, no thrust, no Faraday-probe beam current, no divergence, no efficiency.
Only V_D and I_D are shown; the products computed in digitized_fig4 are this lane's arithmetic.

extraction.value: error bars from several repeated shots, attributed to thermal issues of the HET and the ICP neutralizer

extraction.quantity: ion energy at the ion-collecting electrode
extraction.value: V_ICP - V_K ~ 140 (ICP ions); V_A - V_K ~ 220 (HET ions lost to the electrode)
extraction.note: Authors' sheath-energy estimates at the largest V_D.

extraction.value: the stainless-steel electrode is sputtered; metallic films found after the experiment on part of the glass tube (at the electrode slit) and on the insulators at the HET front
extraction.note: Authors: the negative cathode potential 'has to be minimized in future research and development'.

extraction.quantity: operating duration, lifetime or erosion rate
extraction.note: No run duration, no mass-loss, no life test.

extraction.value: RF plasma turned on first, then V_D applied
extraction.note: No ignition statistics, restart count or cycle data reported.

extraction.value: authors state the ICP neutralizer 'is operational for various gas species including chemically active gases such as water, carbon dioxide, and iodine'
extraction.note: A claim in the summary, not demonstrated in this paper (argon only); no N2/O2 data.

stated_limitations.text: argon only; proof of principle of ion acceleration (p. 2)
poor RF power transfer efficiency (~10 %) caused by eddy-current heating of the ion-collecting electrode; proper electrode design required (p. 8)

enhanced cathodic sheath voltage at large V_D: significant energy loss to ions accelerated by the cathodic sheath; sputtering of the electrode and metallic coating of glass and HET insulators (p. 6, p. 9)
the physics of the broadened IEDF (CEX vs ionization in the potential gradient) is not resolved; 'more detailed measurements will be required' (p. 6)
'more detailed physical studies and development are required to optimize the thruster design and performance' (p. 9)
thermal issues of the HET and ICP neutralizer cause shot-to-shot scatter (p. 7)

derived.q: gas utilization factor U_e = I_a / (0.73 A per mg/s x mdot) at the 3.3 A point
derived.locator: Sec. 3.4 text p. Pb_81 ('0.1 mg/s of the xenon ... is equivalent to 0.073 A', i.e. 0.73 A per mg/s) applied to the reported point
derived.note: SOURCE TYPO: the printed Eq. (1) on p. Pb_81 shows '0.073 [A/mg/s]', which contradicts the same paragraph (0.073 A per 0.1 mg/s) and first principles (e / m_Xe x 1 mg/s = 1.602e-19 C / (131.29 x 1.6605e-27 kg) x 1e-6 kg/s = 0.735 A). This lane uses 0.73 A per mg/s; the literal Eq. (1) constant would give ~151, ten times too high. Consistent with the text statement that the outer-coil U_e is 'comparable to that for the hollow cathode' (HCN-252, Fig. 10); the Fig. 10 axis values were not digitized by this lane (verify).

derived.q: electron production cost C_e = (I_a V_a + P_rf) / I_a at the 3.3 A point
derived.locator: Eq. (2) p. Pb_81 applied to the reported point

derived.q: RF power per ampere at the 3.3 A point
